platform.linuxBackend: gtk3 build tag (GTK 3.24.33 + WebKit2GTK 4.1 2.50.4); untagged GTK4 build needs GtkFileDialog = GTK >= 4.10, Ubuntu 22.04 ships 4.6.9
platform.keyringDep: github.com/zalando/go-keyring v0.2.8 (wincred on Windows, Security.framework on macOS, Secret Service/D-Bus on Linux)

apiSurface.events: app.Event.Emit/On/Once/Off; window.EmitEvent; CustomEvent/WindowEvent cancellable via event.Cancel()
apiSurface.services: application.NewService[T](instance); ServiceStartup(ctx,ServiceOptions) error; ServiceShutdown() error — reverse registration order, after OnShutdown, before PostShutdown
apiSurface.closeToHide: window.RegisterHook(events.Common.WindowClosing, cancel+Hide) — eventHooks run synchronously before eventListeners (incl. internal markAsDestroyed), HandleWindowEvent returns early on cancel
apiSurface.assets: application.AssetOptions{Handler http.Handler, Middleware Middleware, DisableLogging}; Middleware func(next http.Handler) http.Handler + ChainMiddleware

senderContract.bindingIdentity: ctx.Value(application.WindowKey).(application.Window).ID() — native; x-wails-window-id / x-wails-window-name headers are OVERWRITTEN per-request in webViewAssetRequest.Header() (application.go ~L385) so forged client headers cannot win on the desktop webview path
senderContract.navigationVeto: NONE in beta.27 — external-page defense is AssetServer Middleware origin allowlist (empty, http://wails.local, wails://wails, http://wails.localhost) + window-id gate; navigated-away pages carry a real window id but are denied at origin layer; no CurrentURL() getter exists
senderContract.capabilityIssuance: media capability bound to {windowID, token}; grant requires header window id == issued id AND token match AND not revoked

mediaRoute.surface: AssetOptions.Handler mux inside internal wails scheme — NO TCP listener
mediaRoute.bound: http.MaxBytesReader 10 MiB -> 413 above bound; at-bound OK
mediaRoute.roundtrip: POST /media/wav stores raw bytes; GET /media/wav/{id} returns audio/wav byte-identical (sha256 match) — no JSON/base64 expansion
mediaRoute.cancellation: webViewAssetRequest.Context() preserves native cancellation; download write honours r.Context() (cancelled download test passes)
mediaRoute.adapterSignature: native route = standard http.Handler; capability check reads x-wails-window-id header + X-Diva-Media-Token header; response = raw bytes or typed error status
mediaRoute.peakMemory: measured: live-heap delta 22.39 MiB for a 10 MiB upload (~2.2x payload: request body + store entry; a base64 expansion would exceed it). Test TestMediaRoutePeakMemoryAtBound asserts <40 MiB

lifetime.closeToHide: RegisterHook cancel verified by reading eventHooks-before-listeners semantics in webview_window.go:366; runtime exercise verified on Windows x64 (w0-2): window X and taskkill WM_CLOSE both hide, process + runtime survive
lifetime.singleInstance: OnSecondInstanceLaunch callback wired but UNREACHABLE in practice (w0-2): Compose() opens the sealed host before the Wails app exists, so the organism lease rejects instance 2 (-32086) before SingleInstance can arm; single-workspace enforcement is proven via the lease on both platforms; reopen-via-second-launch therefore cannot work
lifetime.trayReopen: Windows x64 (w0-2): tray icon present ('DIVA desktop') but unattached — no AttachWindow/SetMenu → click inert, no menu; hidden window has no user-facing reopen path
lifetime.explicitQuit: Windows x64 (w0-2): no UI quit affordance; graceful quit proven via CTRL_BREAK → 'Quitting application...' → speech teardown joins inflight under CloseBudget → 'teardown complete' → lease released, immediate relaunch opens
